class: An asynchronous shadow dropdown requires its own filter input and scoped offered options
symptom: After custom-button recognition was corrected, ADP still left State blank and repeatedly reported no matching option. Source selection uses the same async widget.
site: ADP Church Mutual application 548, requisition 5001218033006; supervised continuation on 25 October 2026
root_cause: Generic keyboard typing targets the trigger rather than sdf-select-simple's internal filter input. The async option list remains empty or unfiltered. Filtering a known synonym literally can also remove the offered equivalent (Mobile versus Cell).
why_tests_missed: Previous ADP tests mocked open_picker/select_option methods that the PageAgent choice path never called, and ordinary dropdown tests supplied their choices synchronously.
fix: Add an optional portal choice hook supplied with the shared matcher and guarded click function. ADP scopes to the trigger's sdf-select-simple host, matches currently visible options first, fills that host's filter when needed, waits within a fixed budget, clicks a matching offered option and verifies the committed trigger text. Unhandled widgets continue through generic logic; recognized unsuccessful selections do not guess.
prevention: Test the actual caller-to-adapter contract against an async shadow-DOM widget. Scope both filtering and option selection to the current widget; share answer equivalence rules and verify the committed answer.
